tEn: Building Beautiful Websites with Claude: James McDonald's Process
tZh: 用 Claude 打造精美网站：James McDonald 的设计流程
sEn: James McDonald reveals how he uses Claude and MCP to build animated, story-driven websites and elevate his visual design craft.
sZh: James McDonald 分享他如何借助 Claude 与 MCP 打造带动效、重叙事的网站，并提升视觉设计功力。

consensus.en: AI tools like Claude empower designers to build animations and prototypes without engineering background.
consensus.zh: 像 Claude 这样的 AI 工具让没有工程背景的设计师也能构建动画和原型。

consensus.en: Figma remains essential for high-level layout and visual exploration; Claude handles animation and interaction details.
consensus.zh: Figma 仍然是高层布局和视觉探索的必备工具；Claude 负责动画和交互细节。

consensus.en: Building custom mini-tools with AI accelerates creative exploration and iteration.
consensus.zh: 用 AI 构建自定义小工具能加速创意探索和迭代。

consensus.en: Designers should embrace AI to expand their skill set and take ownership of output.
consensus.zh: 设计师应拥抱 AI 来扩展技能并掌控产出。

consensus.en: AI helps spot edge cases and design comprehensive user experiences.
consensus.zh: AI 有助于发现边缘情况并设计全面的用户体验。

consensus.en: The ability to animate and prototype ideas quickly is a game-changer for visual designers.
consensus.zh: 快速制作动画和原型的能力对视觉设计师来说是颠覆性的。

contrarian.en: Designers don't need to be technical to build functional apps; AI can guide the process.
contrarian.zh: 设计师不需要懂技术就能构建可用的应用；AI 可以引导过程。

contrarian.en: Randomness in tools and prompts can lead to unexpected creative breakthroughs.
contrarian.zh: 工具和提示中的随机性可以带来意想不到的创意突破。

contrarian.en: Self-plagiarizing old ideas that didn't work can be repurposed successfully with AI.
contrarian.zh: 将未成功的旧想法自我抄袭，借助 AI 可以成功重新利用。

contrarian.en: Building throwaway tools for specific tasks is more efficient than general prototyping.
contrarian.zh: 为特定任务构建一次性工具比通用原型更高效。

contrarian.en: AI can generate better female faces than male faces, revealing biases in training data.
contrarian.zh: AI 生成女性面孔比男性面孔更好，揭示了训练数据中的偏见。

contrarian.en: Designers should design edge cases even if they seem unlikely, to ensure quality.
contrarian.zh: 设计师应该设计边缘情况，即使它们看似不太可能，以确保质量。

turns.en: It just gives you the freedom to explore something that you might not be able to fully do in Figma. When I've been working with engineers, I would have to almost do storyboarding of how I want the animations to look and feel. But just being able to hand it one artboard or whatever and link it through the MCP, tell it what I want it to do, and then you've got an 11 out of 10 idea that you can then just massage.
turns.zh: 它给了你自由去探索一些你在 Figma 里可能无法完全做到的东西。以前和工程师合作时，我几乎得先做故事板，说明我希望动画看起来和感觉起来是什么样。但现在，我只要把一个画板之类的东西交给它，通过 MCP 链接起来，告诉它我想让它做什么，然后你就得到一个 11 分（满分 10 分）的想法，接着只需打磨它。

turns.en: Welcome to Dive Club. My name is Red and this is where designers never stop learning. This week's episode is with James McDonald, who's easily one of my favorite visual designers on the planet. So I'm always looking for an excuse to have him on the show just to see how he works. So he's going to give us a little behind the scenes of his process and what he's experimenting with today. And the goal is to try to learn what it takes to reach this top-tier of craft.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Dive Club。我是 Red，这里是设计师永不停歇的学习之地。本周的嘉宾是 James McDonald，他无疑是我最喜欢的视觉设计师之一。所以我总是找借口请他上节目，就为了看看他是怎么工作的。他会带我们稍微看看他工作流程的幕后，以及他今天在尝试什么。我们的目标是试着了解要达到这种顶级工艺水平需要什么。

turns.en: If you follow me on Twitter, you know I like to share the projects that I'm working on. So this is for one of my clients, Access Card, and they're a company that basically make mobile wallet credentials easily on your device to access buildings and apartments and just all that fun stuff. I've been tasked to—the existing homepage right now is basically just a sort of landing as a launchpad to get into different parts of the company, the website to find out different parts of the company and stuff like that. But it doesn't really do a good job right now when you first arrive there. So this is the goal—the plan was to sort of come up with a new homepage for this. My Figma files are also just as messy.
turns.zh: 如果你在 Twitter 上关注我，就知道我喜欢分享我正在做的项目。这是为我的一个客户 Access Card 做的，他们是一家让移动钱包凭证轻松存入你设备、用来进入大楼和公寓之类的公司。我接到的任务是——现有的首页基本上只是一个落地页，作为进入公司不同部分、网站不同区域的跳板，用来了解公司的各个部分之类的。但你刚到达那里时，它现在做得并不好。所以这就是目标——计划是为这个做一个新的首页。我的 Figma 文件也一样乱。

turns.en: No, that's pretty clean. I'm not going to lie.
turns.zh: 不，那挺干净的。我不骗你。

turns.en: I mean, again, you can see where it sort of tails off, you know, and it gets to like here and it's like—
turns.zh: 我是说，你又能看到它在哪里逐渐变少，你知道，到这里就有点像——

turns.en: I kind of go in this linear fashion of—and also for more context, it almost looks as if this is in a good position from the start, you know, like this doesn't really change much. But that's because previously I had designed, obviously, a bunch of the other pages for the website. It was just really a homepage they didn't really have, which was a different approach, but it wasn't really required at the time. But now, obviously, we want to do a lot more storytelling and highlighting a lot more features on the homepage. So that's why we've sort of done this kind of full circle background to the homepage. So you will notice this is probably in a good spot already, but it's just because we obviously designed a bunch of these—a bunch of the visual design—previously. A lot of these, trying different layouts like for this, you know, like—I'll show you the live version in a second—but like these kind of cubes. I get the rough idea in there. And this is quite fun actually as well. So this pattern is already on the previous design work that I did a few months ago. I really wanted to try and make that a part of the branding and throughout the website.
turns.zh: 我有点按这种线性的方式来做——另外补充一下背景，它看起来好像从一开始就处于不错的位置，你知道，这部分其实没怎么变。但那是因为之前我显然已经设计了网站上其他一堆页面。他们其实只是缺一个首页，那是一种不同的做法，但当时并不是真的需要。但现在，显然我们想在首页上做更多的叙事、突出更多功能。所以这就是为什么我们给首页做了这种环绕式的背景。所以你会注意到这大概已经处于不错的位置了，但那只是因为我们之前显然已经设计了一堆这些——一堆视觉设计。很多这些，尝试不同的布局，比如这个，你知道，像——我马上给你看线上版本——但像这些方块。我把大致想法放进去了。这个其实也挺好玩的。所以这个图案已经出现在我几个月前做的之前的设计工作里了。我真的很想把它变成品牌的一部分，贯穿整个网站。

turns.en: Let me just jump into the actual project itself.
turns.zh: 让我直接进入实际项目本身吧。

turns.en: Like the existing homepage, you know, it's literally just a heading, some subtext, and then you can watch a video about what Access Grid does and it kind of tells you a bit about them. And then you go into these different use case pages, which—and again, you'll notice a lot of the design language is there already. This is the new one that I've actually been building in Claude, which has been so much fun and sort of invigorating. All the animations and stuff I've built—
turns.zh: 就像现有的首页，你知道，它真的只是一个标题、一些副文本，然后你可以看一个关于 Access Grid 做什么的视频，它稍微介绍了一下他们。然后你进入这些不同的用例页面，这些——你又会注意到很多设计语言已经在那里了。这是我实际上一直在 Claude 里构建的新版本，这真的非常有趣，也让人振奋。所有动画之类的东西都是我构建的——

turns.en: All that—
turns.zh: 所有那些——

turns.en: In Claude. Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: 在 Claude 里。对，对。

turns.en: Kind of crazy, right?
turns.zh: 有点疯狂，对吧？

turns.en: That's kind of crazy.
turns.zh: 是有点疯狂。

turns.en: It's wild. And I have noticed even just over the last few weeks, like Opus 5.5 is even just—if you just tell the agent or the LLM what you want to do, I've really noticed that it does such a great job right away initially. Previously, it would do something that maybe would apply some motion like too quick or too slow or just always felt as if you had to get in there and really tweak a lot of the stuff. But the hero I probably messed about with quite a lot—how the H1 and the sub copy staggers in and then the device comes in. But yeah, I wanted that to sort of mimic almost like putting your phone up against a reader. Like, you know, like that sort of tapping it against something. So that's what I went for there.
turns.zh: 太野了。我注意到，甚至就在过去几周，Opus 5.5 甚至——如果你直接告诉智能体或 LLM 你想做什么，我真的注意到它一开始就做得非常好。以前，它做的东西可能会应用一些动效，要么太快要么太慢，或者总感觉你得进去真正调整一大堆东西。但 hero 部分我大概调了很多——H1 和副文案怎么错开进入，然后设备进来。但没错，我想让那个几乎模仿把手机贴到读卡器上的感觉。就像，你知道，那种把它轻触到某个东西上的感觉。所以那就是我在那里追求的效果。

turns.en: Real quick message and then we can jump back into it. All right, big news. You can now use Jitter inside Claude, Codex, Grok Bot, or wherever you work using the all new Jitter MCP. I mean, I've always said that Jitter makes animating easier than any other tool out there, but this takes it to a whole other level. Like, you can be in a meeting about some kind of an upcoming product launch and have Jitter immediately start exploring animated social posts right after it ends. Or you can even adapt your designs to different aspect ratios in a single prompt. And everything the MCP creates is a native Jitter file. So you're not just stuck with another video export that you have to prompt from scratch. You can easily hop in and fine-tune your animations by hand. It's just another reason why Jitter is my go-to tool for animation. So if you want to give the new MCP a try, head to dive.club/jitter.
turns.zh: 先来一条短消息，然后我们继续。好消息。你现在可以在 Claude、Codex、Grok Bot 里，或者任何你工作的地方，通过全新的 Jitter MCP 使用 Jitter。我一直说 Jitter 让动画制作比市面上任何其他工具都更容易，但这把它提升到了另一个层次。比如，你可以正在开一个关于即将发布产品的会，会议一结束就让 Jitter 立刻开始探索动画社交帖子。或者你甚至可以在一个提示里把设计适配到不同的宽高比。而且 MCP 创建的一切都是原生 Jitter 文件。所以你不只是被另一个视频导出困住、还得从头提示。你可以轻松进去手动微调动画。这只是 Jitter 是我动画首选工具的又一个原因。所以如果你想试试新的 MCP，请前往 dive.club/jitter。

turns.en: There's only one app on my computer that I use literally hundreds of times per day and it's Raycast. And now that they have dictation built right into Raycast 2.0, my usage has gone to a whole other level. I literally canceled my Super Whisper subscription because it's that good. The design is as elegant as you'd expect from the Raycast team, but there are some seriously powerful features that really take it to the next level. And one of my favorites is styles. It allows you to set up custom instructions for specific apps and websites. So I can get clean prompts when I'm building in code or even automatically structure my output as markdown when I'm dictating the dive newsletter. It's just another reason why Raycast is the very first thing I recommend installing on a computer. So if you're somehow not using it already, head to dive.club/raycast to sign up.
turns.zh: 我电脑上只有一个应用我每天真的会用上几百次，那就是 Raycast。现在他们把听写功能直接内置到 Raycast 2.0 里，我的使用量又上了一个全新的层次。我真的取消了 Super Whisper 订阅，因为它就是那么好。设计一如既往地优雅，符合你对 Raycast 团队的期待，但还有一些非常强大的功能真正把它提升到下一个层次。我最喜欢的功能之一是样式。它允许你为特定应用和网站设置自定义指令。所以我在写代码时可以得到干净的提示，甚至在口述 Dive 通讯时自动把输出结构化为 markdown。这只是 Raycast 是我推荐在电脑上安装的第一个东西的又一个原因。所以如果你不知怎么还没在用，请前往 dive.club/raycast 注册。

turns.en: Now on to the episode. I think one of the things that I admire about your work is you're really good at finding these little patterns or visual motifs that you then pull on and extrapolate into the rest of the brand. And I think this—even the way that you have this little grid and you have the connectors inside of it.
turns.zh: 现在进入正片。我欣赏你作品的一点是，你非常擅长找到这些小图案或视觉母题，然后把它们延展、外推到品牌的其余部分。我觉得这个——甚至你有的这个小网格，以及里面的连接线。

transcript.sec: Designing the Access Grid brand element

turns.en: Can you talk a little bit about that part of the creative process? Because everything else is standard layout, right? But it's that part that makes it really stand out.
turns.zh: 你能稍微讲讲创作过程中的那一部分吗？因为其他部分都是标准布局，对吧？但正是那一部分让它真正脱颖而出。

turns.en: That part on here was designed — and the original, you can see it in the background here — it was done with the grid work. Even here, this is all static. It's a combination of the blue in the background here, and then it's all matrixed out into the white. That was what I was kind of trying to go for. And there's no real thinking behind that — I was just inspired by that sort of design language and I tried to make that the brand element for Access Grid. So obviously being able to take that a bit further was like, how do I bring that into Claude and just see where it takes me, you know? So this was where I started. I bought this tool — I can't really remember, it's been a while since I've opened this — but I wanted to make sure that... I think this was the hero size and I added a few different presets in there. But yeah, this was one of the original tools for this, and I basically wanted to try — you know how in the logo here there are these weird L shapes? It's a combination of the L shapes. That's where that idea came from, to try and animate those, just to again reinforce the brand. And this is where it started: I bought this little tool where I can just draw these anywhere and then it will start trying to draw the L-shapes, and you can mess about with the stroke width. Are they solid? Are they dashed? You know, you can randomize a bunch of this stuff as well. I don't know if you'll love doing that, but anytime I make these tools, I love to add a random button, because sometimes you can just get weird stuff happening.
turns.zh: 这里这一部分是我设计的——原始版本你可以在这儿的背景里看到——是用网格做出来的。就算在这里，这也全是静态的。它是背景里这种蓝色的组合，然后全部矩阵式地过渡到白色。这就是我大致想追求的效果。这背后其实没有太多深思熟虑——我只是被那种设计语言启发了，然后试着把它做成 Access Grid 的品牌元素。所以显然，能把它再推进一步就是：我怎么把它带进 Claude，看看它会把我带到哪里，你懂吧？这就是我的起点。我买了这个工具——我记不太清了，好久没打开过了——但我想确保……我记得这是主视觉尺寸，我在里面加了几个不同的预设。不过没错，这是最早做这个的工具之一，我基本上是想试试——你看这 logo 里这些奇怪的 L 形？它是这些 L 形的组合。那个想法就是从这儿来的，试着给它们做动画，同样是为了强化品牌。这就是起点：我买了这个小工具，我可以随便在哪里画这些，然后它就会开始试着画出 L 形，你还可以调整描边宽度。是实线？是虚线？你知道的，你还可以随机化一堆这些东西。我不知道你会不会喜欢这么做，但每次我做这些工具，我都喜欢加一个随机按钮，因为有时候你就是能弄出些奇怪的东西来。

turns.en: I even do it in my prompts sometimes. I'm like, "Do these three concepts that I want, and then also just do two concepts that I'm not thinking of."
turns.zh: 我有时候在提示词里也会这么干。我会说：“做这三个我想要的概念，然后再做两个我没想到的概念。”

turns.en: Can you imagine?
turns.zh: 你能想象吗？

turns.en: Honestly, 18 months ago, if you saw this — if this was part of your design process, the idea of building a tool — I mean, you're the person that for the longest time I associated with just sweating the details of every little custom vector in Figma. And now you're hitting a random button in a custom tool that you built yourself.
turns.zh: 说实话，18 个月前，如果你看到这个——如果这是你设计流程的一部分，自己造工具这个想法——我是说，很长一段时间里，我联想到的你，就是那个在 Figma 里为每一个小自定义矢量抠细节的人。而现在你在自己造的工具里按随机按钮。

turns.en: Yeah, it's crazy. Even like 6 months ago. Like honestly, I feel like I'm sort of a late bloomer when it comes to this stuff, because like —
turns.zh: 是啊，太疯狂了。甚至 6 个月前都还是这样。说实话，我觉得在这件事上我算是大器晚成的那种，因为——

turns.en: I wasn't going to say it. I'm glad you did.
turns.zh: 我可没打算这么说。还好你自己说了。

turns.en: No, I'm 100%. And so it disheartens me when I see designers sort of not being all in on this stuff, because I know I felt that way, you know, like where it was kind of intimidating to think beyond Figma — like, can I apply my skill set in a way that will benefit the work that I'm doing? And I think this is just — even just this really simple example — but if I was just designing this in Figma, you can always visualize it to a certain degree, to a certain point, you know? But just like — I know the animation for this is probably too quick, but that's where you use your design mind to say, "Right, okay, I understand this is animating in too quick here. How do I build a tool that then helps me massage those details, you know?" So that's essentially what I try and do when I'm building any of these little mini tools, if you like. You can slow down how these draw, how they exit, they sort of blur into a fade. You can do things like —
turns.zh: 不，我百分百同意。所以当我看到设计师们没有全身心投入这件事时，我会挺沮丧的，因为我知道我自己也有过那种感觉，你知道的，就是想到 Figma 之外的东西会觉得有点吓人——比如，我能不能把我的技能用在能让我手头工作受益的地方？我觉得这就是——哪怕只是这个非常简单的例子——但如果我只是在 Figma 里设计这个，你总能在某种程度上、到某个程度为止把它可视化出来，你知道吧？但就像——我知道这个的动画可能太快了，但这时候你就得用你的设计思维说：“好，我明白这里动画进来得太快了。那我怎么造一个工具，帮我打磨这些细节，你懂吧？”所以这基本上就是我在做任何这些小工具时想做的事。你可以放慢它们绘制的方式、退出的方式，它们会模糊成淡出。你可以做这些——

turns.en: Did you give Claude one pattern example in an SVG and then just tell it to trace it? Because even that tracing animation is really good. I'm wondering what it took to arrive there.
turns.zh: 你是给 Claude 一个 SVG 的图案示例，然后让它照着描吗？因为就连那个描边动画都做得非常好。我很好奇做到那一步花了多少功夫。

turns.en: I honestly don't even know if I'd do that. I think I just gave it the sort of pattern that was in the Figma. So I think I just gave it something like this. I drew this in Figma, you know, and I think I just pointed it — I pointed it to just this section and was like, the pattern in the background — I want to make a pattern generator that helps build this. I think for the most part it was probably a few prompts for this sort of tool, you know, because there's nothing really to it. It's something just to help visualize what I was trying to achieve in the actual real build. This was actually a fun one. This was pre-Figma, before I even started designing in Figma. I was trying to build out how we can evolve the existing Access Grid work that I had done already, and I was like, how do I try and build on the branding as such. So I actually love this tool. It ended up evolving into something that probably won't get used for Access Grid, but it's something that I could maybe revert back to for inspiration. Again, just outputs like random —
turns.zh: 说实话，我都不确定我是不是那么做的。我想我只是把 Figma 里的那种图案给了它。所以我想我只是给了它类似这样的东西。这是我在 Figma 里画的，你知道的，然后我想我只是把它指出来——我指向了这一段，说背景里的这个图案——我想做一个图案生成器来帮忙构建这个。我想大部分情况下，这类工具大概几个提示词就出来了，你知道的，因为它其实没什么复杂的。它只是帮我把我在实际构建中想达到的效果可视化出来。这个其实挺有意思的。这是 Figma 之前的，在我开始在 Figma 里设计之前。我当时在试着构建我们如何演进我已经做好的 Access Grid 作品，然后我想，我怎么在品牌上继续做文章。所以我其实很喜欢这个工具。它最后演变成了一个可能不会用在 Access Grid 上的东西，但它是我可以回头找灵感的东西。又是，就是输出些随机的——

turns.en: Crazy, fun things like this.
turns.zh: 像这样疯狂、好玩的东西。

turns.en: I don't have any idea how it's doing this, but — because it wasn't the original intention for this certain generator, this pattern generator. I wanted something like this, where it took the Access Grid logo and it was building out — it was using vertical lines. I think you can change the color here. You can use a custom color. Originally this was the idea for this, but then I think I even started playing around with — when you click this, maybe that's not a good color. Let's see. Yeah, so when you click it, it just ripples different effects. What's this? Yeah, you can just mess about. I did all these different parameters so you can just do fun, different patterns, you know, and this is how I like to start projects now — just adding a bunch of this stuff, you know, just to see where it takes you. It's just endless possibilities of inspiration. turns.en: Can you talk at a high level about how this impacts your creativity? Because it's almost like you're discovering parts of the visual language rather than manually exploring them on their own. Like what is that actually like at a human level? What does it even change for your own process?
turns.zh: 你能从宏观层面谈谈这对你的创造力有什么影响吗？因为这几乎就像你在发现视觉语言的一部分，而不是手动去探索它们。从人的层面来说，那到底是什么感觉？它甚至改变了你自己的流程吗？

turns.en: Honestly, I think that's the friction point for someone like myself who's never really had an engineering background, who's never built their own websites. I've always handed design files off to engineers. I think just discovering ideas and inspiration doing it this way, it empowers a lot of that process. So, like I said, you could start with a really simple idea—this default one here was I took the shape and I wanted to try to find a way to explore how that shape could be viewed in a different way. So the idea here was this area here would be the hero or part of a section that might be under the hero, or just a way to bring the branding into the website or the design. So you might see a different version of this, and then another idea comes to mind and you just try to build that out as well. And then before you know it, there's just this weird combination of things that you've built—I'm not saying the random buttons like the BO and end though, but a bunch of this stuff could quite easily be seen in some sort of brand guideline book for a new design. So yeah, I think a lot of this stuff is where I definitely had a lot of apprehension about exploring and playing around with these different tools like Claude's, and obviously you've got Codex now as well and different tooling. I think just starting with something simple and a simple idea can really evolve really quickly. I've always found before all this tooling and AI or whatever, and Figma, that's the part that took the longest, especially building out website design and landing pages. I think it really does just help evolve the idea and try to build out different examples of that idea that you might have inside Figma. So yeah, that's kind of how I like to think about it.
turns.zh: 老实说，我觉得那正是像我这样没有工程背景、从未自己建过网站的人的摩擦点。我一直是把设计文件交给工程师。我觉得用这种方式发现想法和灵感，能赋能很多这样的过程。所以就像我说的，你可以从一个非常简单的想法开始——这里的默认版本就是我拿了这个形状，想尝试找到一种方式来探索这个形状如何能以不同方式被看待。所以这里的想法是，这个区域会成为主视觉区，或者主视觉区下方某个部分的一部分，或者只是一种将品牌带入网站或设计的方式。但通过这样做，你通过要求它构建不同的参数，创造了所有这些不同的探索。所以你可能会看到这个的不同版本，然后另一个想法浮现，你就试着把它也构建出来。然后不知不觉中，就有了这种奇怪的组合——我不是说像 BO 和 end 那样的随机按钮，但很多东西你很容易就能在某种品牌指南书中看到，比如为新设计准备的。所以是的，我觉得很多东西正是我对于探索和摆弄这些不同工具（比如 Claude，显然你现在还有 Codex 以及不同的工具）有很多顾虑的地方。我觉得从简单的东西和简单的想法开始，真的可以非常快地演变。在所有这类工具和 AI 之前，还有 Figma，我一直发现那部分耗时最长，尤其是构建网站设计和落地页。真的就是试图找到那个核心想法，而我觉得这些工具能帮助你更快地推进这个过程。至少对我来说是这样。我觉得它真的能帮助演变想法，并尝试构建出你在 Figma 中可能有的那个想法的不同示例。所以是的，这大概就是我喜欢思考它的方式。

turns.zh: 我来自纯设计背景——从 Photoshop 到 Sketch 再到 Figma。我从未真正亲手构建过自己的作品。所以能够摆弄这些东西，并看到事物变为现实，对我来说是最棒的感觉。太有趣了。我喜欢做这些事，我认为它可以提升，尤其是网页作品。我只是觉得，如果你大量设计这些东西，你真的可以提升很多。

turns.zh: 是的，所以我觉得这个想法——我想这是几个月前的事了。我只是想找一个机会真正全力以赴：我现在真的能自己建一个网站吗？真的能自己建一个应用吗？我在 Twitter 等地方关注的一些人在做这个，我就想我要试一试。所以显然我从应用本身开始，就像——如果你把 Ring 门铃摄像头连接到你的应用里，你就能看到它们，这显然是在 Mac 上快速查看你拥有的门铃的一种方式。所以是的，我想显然是从 Figma 开始的。

turns.zh: 这就像我最初想要的氛围。很多这些东西来自 Cosmos。我经常用 Cosmos 找灵感。我很确定很多设计师都知道——很多人用那个。

turns.zh: 或者我喜欢它。它真的很棒，能让你找到很多你正在寻找的相似的 relatable 的东西。我不知道他们怎么做到的，但太不可思议了。显然我最初想走这种 90 年代摄像机感觉的路线。老实说，我现在有点希望我走了这条路。我不知道为什么我切换了。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. I basically was trying to come up with fun videos, short videos—I think it was Midjourney actually that I was building short clips of just random front door scenes from the 90s, but I just thought I can't put that on the website because people are going to think, you know, what is this technology? turns.zh: 是的，是的。我基本上是在尝试制作有趣的视频，短视频——我想实际上是 Midjourney，我在构建一些 90 年代随机前门场景的短片，但我只是想我不能把它放在网站上，因为人们会想，你知道，这是什么技术？这家伙受到威胁——嗯，所以我想那就是我停下来的地方。

turns.zh: 是的，就像它在 Midjourney 中输出的一些片段很搞笑。它就是不能——我没能让它正常工作。所以那是我构建的第一件事——我想这是在——我不记得我在哪里做了这张图。可能也是 Midjourney。显然我喜欢 Shed US 的人。他们的网站真的很酷。我追求那种奇怪的——很多东西都是随手丢弃的。我最终没有走这条路。所以这显然是实际应用本身的设计。我只是试图保持非常简单。还有很多东西我很想添加，但这里的很多 UI 只是非常非常简单，非常基础。但都是定制的——很多图标是定制的。我只是想尝试构建一些我自己会用的东西，以及我能快速完成的东西，因为我以前从未构建过 Mac 应用。我不知道那需要什么。我不知道我需要一个 Apple 开发者账户。就像我在经历这些。我想，哦，我需要这个东西。好的。

turns.en: How was the process? Talk to us a little bit about—was it easier than you thought, harder than you thought? Did you get stuck places? Like people who are also like 'I've never done anything'—if James can do it, maybe I can. What was it like?
turns.zh: 过程怎么样？跟我们谈谈——是比你想象的容易，还是更难？你有没有卡住的地方？就像那些也说“我从未做过任何事”的人——如果 James 能做到，也许我也能。那是什么感觉？

turns.en: Yeah. A lot of it, honestly, I just asked Claude to help me and guide me through it. I just kept asking it things like, what would I need to build this app? And it would give me a list, and then I would almost treat that list like multiple lists, so I would start somewhere, build it out, try to get through a to-do list, and then I would take the next thing. A lot of that stuff I literally was just asking Claude, like is this going to be secure? I don't know how this works. Give me all the information I need to know about how to build this app. But the Ring API that it works from has a lot of that stuff baked in already. From that standpoint, I was kind of just saying, okay, give me some ideas for the layout, what sort of settings that I might need. And then I just came back into Figma and I was just building around them. So really obscure cases like this, for example, some cameras are battery powered. That's where this stuff is. Obviously there'll be cases where your camera goes offline. So how does that design look? Again, this was some other design examples of the batteries or whatever. Can't quite remember if this was the battery, I'm not sure. But yeah, a lot of this and then just designing a lot of this stuff, how it might look with different icons. Yeah, so I think this was just from Claude.
turns.zh: 是的。老实说，很多地方我只是让 Claude 帮助我并指导我完成。我一直问它类似的问题，比如，我需要什么来构建这个应用？它会给我一个列表，然后我几乎把那个列表当作多个列表，所以我会从某个地方开始，构建出来，试着完成一个待办事项列表，然后我再做下一件事。所以我认为很多这些东西——我真的很想确保应用是安全的，没有人能看到你的摄像头和你的家之类的。很多这些东西我真的只是问 Claude，比如这安全吗？我不知道这是如何工作的。给我所有我需要知道的关于如何构建这个应用的信息。但它使用的 Ring API 已经内置了很多这些东西。从这个角度来说，我只是说，好的，给我一些布局的想法，我可能需要什么样的设置。然后我回到 Figma，我只是围绕它们构建。所以像这样非常 obscure 的情况，例如，有些摄像头是电池供电的。这就是这些东西所在。显然会有你的摄像头离线的情况。那么设计看起来如何？再次，这是一些其他设计示例，比如电池之类的。不太记得这是不是电池，我不确定。但是是的，很多这些，然后只是设计很多这些东西，它可能看起来如何与不同的图标。是的，所以我认为这只是来自 Claude。

turns.en: This is probably the proudest part that I'm most grateful for, actually. We obviously can do a bunch of things with animation and everything, but it's so unbelievable—it's spotting the edge cases that I would miss.

Referencing the Figma file back and forth, telling it to point to certain parts of the UI like this part of bringing this UI here. This was like the before the access grid stuff. This was definitely the first project where you've just building out the buttons and stuff, the animations.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这就是为什么我经历了设计一堆这些东西的痛苦。但一旦我有了一个好的起点——这个没有很多边缘情况——Claude 在复制很多 UI 方面做得很好，你懂的？所以还好。我最终不必设计一堆东西。比如这个视图基本上就是当你收到警报时，它会告诉你，你可以滚动这个列表，并重放，比如如果有人敲你的门之类的。很多这些东西都很有趣，比如为实际的实时视图设计这些图标。是的，比如这里，我设计了，你知道，如果你点击麦克风图标，那是一个小光晕，会根据音量或其他什么移动。你管那叫什么？我不知道技术术语，但它就是很好玩的东西。所以是的，那就是这个应用。是的，网站在这里。网站的东西在这里。这个，就像我的 Figma 是个笑话。东西到处都是。我只想保持简单。很多在实际网站上，显然我们有这种完整的演示，展示某人可能如何使用这个应用。我觉得一些公司已经这样做了，你懂的，但所有这些，设计所有这些东西，构建所有这一切，比如这个光标点击不同相机的小动画。那是我第一次在 Claude 中来回交流，告诉它我到底想要它做什么。来回引用 Figma 文件，告诉它指向 UI 的某些部分，比如把这一部分 UI 带到这里。这是在 access grid 的东西之前。这绝对是我第一个项目，你只是构建按钮之类的，动画。

turns.en: It felt like magic the first time you did that.
turns.zh: 你第一次做的时候感觉像魔法一样。

turns.en: It was.
turns.zh: 确实是。

turns.en: Especially if it was one of your first Claude experiments.
turns.zh: 特别是如果那是你最早的 Claude 实验之一。

turns.en: Yeah, it was like that's it. As if from Midjourney. This is like some of the good examples from Midjourney where it kind of looks half decent, but you can still kind of tell.
turns.zh: 是的，就像那样。就像来自 Midjourney 的。这就像 Midjourney 的一些好例子，看起来还凑合，但你还是能看出来。

turns.en: Even like these animations like kind of loved how this one uh uh
turns.zh: 甚至像这些动画，有点喜欢这个，呃呃

turns.en: Oh, that's cool.
turns.zh: 哦，那很酷。

turns.en: You know, in the Ring app, I don't know if you've got Ring cameras, but in the Ring app, it's got sort of similar UI to this where you can scrub the motion event in the app and to get that to work with this, how this video scrubs back and forth, that was just like magic for me. I kind of think this one took a while to get right. It kept trying to quickly zip through the video file. It kept going away back forth like really fast. But obviously the scrub is meant to be quite slow there. So I think that took a while. And then like this one, but I think I pointed Claude to—I think there was an animation library and I seen a kind of pulse effect like that. And I just pointed it to that and just kind of massage some of the pulse details in the background. There's like a double pulse in the background. And yeah, just things like that, just like really—like I said, this was the first project where I really had fun with that part of it, you know, trying to just take it from zero to one and honestly just so much fun building this stuff and that's where I got a taste for it, you know, like I can actually if I can build this, I can build my own projects now, you know.
turns.zh: 你知道，在 Ring 应用里，我不知道你有没有 Ring 摄像头，但在 Ring 应用里，它有类似的 UI，你可以在应用里拖动运动事件，要让这个工作起来，这个视频如何来回拖动，那对我来说就像魔法一样。我觉得这个花了一段时间才做对。它总是试图快速浏览视频文件。它总是来回移动得非常快。但显然这里的拖动应该是相当慢的。所以我觉得那花了一段时间。然后像这个，但我想我让 Claude 参考了——我想有一个动画库，我看到了那种脉冲效果。我就让它参考那个，然后调整背景中一些脉冲细节。背景中有双重脉冲。是的，就像那样的事情，真的就像我说的，这是我第一个真正享受那部分工作的项目，你知道，试图从零到一，老实说构建这些东西太有趣了，这就是我尝到甜头的地方，你知道，就像如果我能构建这个，我现在就能构建我自己的项目了，你懂的。

turns.en: So, you have a taste. Obviously, you're getting pretty comfortable. Like you're in a groove with Claude. Some of the stuff that you're making is incredible. You're owning a lot of the output that historically would have required an engineering partner. How does this change the way that you think about positioning yourself even as a freelance designer moving forward?
turns.zh: 所以，你尝到甜头了。显然，你变得相当熟练。你和 Claude 配合得很默契。你做的一些东西令人难以置信。你承担了很多历史上需要工程合作伙伴才能完成的输出。这如何改变你对自己作为自由设计师未来定位的思考？

turns.en: I think it's just another skill set to add to your toolkit, you know. I wouldn't try to think about how to position myself in that sense, but a company can hire you to do all, you know. I think that's a bigger benefit not only to them but to yourself. I think it's just like I said, it's just another skill set that you can add to yourself and still very early days, you know, like only been working on a couple of projects, but the fact that it's fun and I actually enjoy it makes a huge difference, you know. I think if I still hated it, I still hated going back and forth and I just only wanted to be in Figma, then of course, but the fact that I actually enjoy it, I actually want to be involved and even thinking about working with different engineers or being able to collaborate with them—I've not had that opportunity yet to do that, but being able to actually be in those conversations with engineers on how you actually build this stuff and be a part of how this stuff comes together is also pretty exciting, you know, like being able to quickly put out these ideas. So, yeah, it definitely opens a lot more doors, you know, to answer your question from a positional sense, you know, I've not really thought about it in great detail. Like I said before, that the Austin at Access Credit gives you a lot of freedom to really explore ideas and he puts a lot of trust in myself to build these ideas and he could have quite easily have said, you know, "I want a veteran engineer to build this," you know, but being able to have that sort of freedom and that trust to build it as well has been so fun and like just last week we set up the code base. So, hopefully soon be able to actually make meaningful change to the website, not just like from a, you know, I've just got a project in Claude, but actually be able to push ideas live, you know, I'm excited about that part as part of it as well.
turns.zh: 我觉得这只是另一种可以加入你工具包的技能，你懂的。我不会试图从那个角度思考如何定位自己，但一家公司可以雇佣你做所有事情，你知道。我认为这对他们和你自己都有更大的好处。我觉得就像我说的，这只是另一种你可以添加到自己的技能，而且还是很早期，你知道，只做了几个项目，但事实上它很有趣，我真的很享受，这带来了巨大的不同，你知道。我想如果我还讨厌它，我还讨厌来回交流，我只想待在 Figma 里，那当然，但事实上我真的很享受，我真的想参与，甚至考虑与不同的工程师合作或能够与他们协作——我还没有机会这样做，但能够真正参与那些与工程师关于如何构建这些东西的对话，并成为这些东西如何组合的一部分，也很令人兴奋，你知道，就像能够快速推出这些想法。所以，是的，它绝对打开了更多的大门，你知道，从定位的角度回答你的问题，你知道，我真的没有详细思考过。就像我之前说的，Access Credit 的 Austin 给了你很多自由去真正探索想法，他非常信任我来构建这些想法，他本可以很容易地说，你知道，“我想要一个资深工程师来构建这个，”你知道，但能够有那种自由和信任来构建它真是太有趣了，就像上周我们建立了代码库。所以，希望很快能够真正对网站做出有意义的改变，不仅仅是从，你知道，我只是在 Claude 里有一个项目，而是真正能够将想法上线，你知道，我对这部分也很兴奋。

turns.en: Is this the first project that you've taken on as a freelancer where you're building it?
turns.zh: 这是你作为自由职业者接的第一个由你构建的项目吗？

turns.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, first one.
turns.zh: 是的，是的，是的，第一个。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Dude, how cool is that?
turns.zh: 老兄，这也太酷了吧？

turns.en: I know, it's so exciting. It's been so much fun. For the longest time, honestly, I was always just so jealous of engineers being able to build ideas — or not even jealous, sometimes frustrated as well, because maybe an engineer doesn't quite do what you envision, you know, the idea that you have in your mind. So being able to actually tangibly put an idea together from zero to one and build them — I think, like I said, it really sort of empowers me to do a lot more of that. And it's just such an exciting time, I think, for designers that are in the same sort of boat as me, where — like I said before — I didn't have an engineering background, who are sort of experimenting with these tools. I've never been a sort of technical designer whatsoever. I think I've mentioned that to you before. Thinking in systems — I'm just not that designer at all. But these tools sort of unlock just a part of the process where, if you're just patient enough to keep playing around and keep trying to bring simple ideas over — I started pretty simple, just trying to build little tools that might help with animating an illustration or whatever, you know, starting there. And then I think the nature of the beast with these tools is things just move fast, and you will move fast — it's inevitable you'll move fast and pick things up and learn how this stuff works. So I'm loving it, you know, it's so enjoyable working on this stuff.
turns.zh: 我知道，太让人兴奋了，真的特别好玩。说实话，很长一段时间里，我一直特别羡慕工程师能把想法做出来——甚至不只是羡慕，有时候还挺沮丧的，因为工程师做出来的东西可能不完全是你设想的样子，不是你脑子里那个想法。所以能真正把一个想法从零到一实打实地做出来、搭起来——我觉得，就像我说的，这真的让我更有能力去做更多这样的事。而且我觉得，对于和我处境相同的设计师来说，现在真是个激动人心的时代——就像我之前说的，我没有工程背景，只是在尝试这些工具。我从来都不是那种技术型设计师，我记得我跟你说过。系统化思维——我根本不是那种设计师。但这些工具解锁了流程中的一部分：只要你足够有耐心，不断去玩、不断去尝试把简单的想法做出来——我一开始做得挺简单的，就是试着做点小工具，可能帮忙给插画做动画之类的，从那儿开始。然后我觉得这些工具的本质就是，事情进展得很快，你也会进展得很快——你必然会快速上手，学会这些东西是怎么运作的。所以我特别享受，真的，做这些东西太有意思了。

turns.en: It's cool, man. I understand the genesis now of your "Things Are Weird" article a little bit more, now that I know that you're in the middle of your first project. To be doing something professionally for so long, to be at the top of the game, and then you're doing something that you've just never done or even imagined yourself packaging as a professional before — it's cool, man. And I find your journey and willingness to jump in and build all these things and even just ask yourself the question of, you know, can I do this? Should I just see if I can build a whole product from scratch?
turns.zh: 太酷了，老兄。现在我更理解你那篇《Things Are Weird》文章的由来了，因为我知道你正处在第一个项目的中途。做一件事做了那么多年，做到行业顶尖，然后去做一件你从没做过、甚至没想过会作为专业人士去打包呈现的事——太酷了，老兄。我很欣赏你的这段旅程，以及你愿意跳进来做这些东西，甚至愿意问自己那个问题：我能做到吗？我是不是该试试看能不能从零做一个完整的产品？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: I think that's the mentality that gets people really far nowadays. So I appreciate you coming on, taking us through the journey, your creative process. I will continue to find excuses to interview you as long as I do this podcast. You're one of my favorite people to be inspired from.
turns.zh: 我觉得正是这种心态让人如今能走得很远。所以谢谢你来做客，带我们走过这段旅程、你的创作过程。只要我还做这个播客，我就会继续找借口采访你。你是我最喜欢从中获得灵感的人之一。

turns.en: I appreciate it. No problem. No, I appreciate it as always.
turns.zh: 谢谢。没问题。不，我一如既往地感谢你。

turns.en: Hey, if you enjoyed this episode, don't forget that every Thursday I go live with Tommy Geoco for Dive Radio, where we deep dive into trending topics and hear from a ton of incredible designers in the industry. So if you want to get that on your calendar, just go to dive.club/radio and I'll see you on Thursdays at 4:00 p.m. Eastern.
turns.zh: 嘿，如果你喜欢这期节目，别忘了每周四我都会和 Tommy Geoco 一起直播 Dive Radio，我们会深入探讨热门话题，并听听业内众多优秀设计师的分享。所以如果你想把它加进日历，就去 dive.club/radio，我们周四美国东部时间下午 4 点见。
